title: Robust self-test of the maximally entangled state of two-qubits without assuming unitary observables
abstract: Standard device-independent self-testing uses Naimark dilation to assume projective measurements, masking the operational limitations of realistic non-unitary observables. We establish a robust pure self-test for the singlet and Pauli observables that entirely circumvents dilation of the measurement apparatus. Assuming a pure state to model an untrusted source, we regularize the physical non-projective operators and derive an analytic $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtε)$ robustness bound. Our results suggest that device-independent certification of real implementations is significantly more demanding than standard projective models imply.
summary: This paper presents a novel self-testing protocol for entangled states that rigorously accounts for non-ideal, non-projective measurements common in real experiments. By regularizing physical observables instead of assuming perfect projective measurements, the authors derive an error bound scaling as $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\epsilon})$. This demonstrates that device-independent certification is significantly harder than standard theoretical models suggest.
main_problem: To develop a robust self-testing protocol for quantum states that accurately accounts for non-projective (non-unitary) measurement observables, overcoming limitations in standard models.
main_result: The authors establish an analytic robustness bound scaling as $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\epsilon})$ for certifying maximally entangled states using real POVMs, showing this is significantly more demanding than projective model predictions.
method: The approach circumvents Naimark dilation by regularizing physical non-projective operators using a modified sign function and deriving error bounds based on spectral decomposition and norm inequalities.
model_or_system: The system involves two qubits sharing a maximally entangled state (Bell scenario), tested via local Pauli observables measured through general Positive Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs).
key_observables: Local physical observables ($A_x, B_y$), the CHSH Bell operator $B$, and the observed probability distribution $p$.
important_parameters: The experimental error parameter $\epsilon$; the robustness bound scales as $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\epsilon})$.
main_assumptions: Standard frameworks assume projectivity; this work explicitly models non-projective POVMs and regularizes them rather than assuming ideal measurement apparatuses.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first identifying the failure of standard dilation methods, then introducing regularization via a modified sign function ($	ext{sgn}^*$), and finally deriving the total error bound by combining the regularization error ($\Delta$) with the bound derived from regularized unitaries.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial refinement to device-independent quantum certification protocols, directly addressing the gap between idealized theoretical models (projective measurements) and realistic experimental limitations (non-unitary POVMs).
